# Green Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
The manifesto addresses cost of living challenges, public service provision, housing, energy, and environmental concerns, proposing increased public investment funded through taxation changes and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care
The party proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing rapid GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability, boosting staff pay, and investing £3bn annually in NHS dentistry by 2030. Mental health services would receive equal footing with physical health, with 28-day access targets for therapies.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, introducing free personal care, establishing career structures for carers with national pay standards, and supporting disabled people through benefit increases.

## Housing
The manifesto commits to 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A retrofit programme would invest £29bn over five years for home insulation and £9bn for heating systems.

## Energy
Proposals include wind providing approximately 70% of UK electricity by 2030, ending new oil and gas licences, removing fossil fuel subsidies, and introducing community ownership requirements for renewable infrastructure. Nuclear power development would cease.

## Economy and Work
The party proposes £40bn average annual investment in green economic transformation, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. Worker proposals include a £15 minimum wage, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, repealing anti-union legislation, and moving toward a four-day working week.

## Welfare
Proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, abolishing the two-child benefit cap, increasing disability benefits by 5%, and ending the five-week benefit wait.

## Taxation
The manifesto proposes a wealth tax (1% on assets above £10m, 2% above £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, reforming inheritance tax, and introducing a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Estimated additional revenue would be £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Environment and Nature
Proposals include a Rights of Nature Act, protecting 30% of land and seas by 2030, bringing water companies into public ownership, and phasing out harmful pesticides. Additional DEFRA funding of £1.5bn would support environmental enforcement.

## Education
Commitments include £8bn school funding increase, £2.5bn annually for building safety, £5bn for SEND provision, scrapping tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport
The party proposes £10bn annual public transport subsidies, free bus travel for under-18s, £2.5bn annually for cycling and walking infrastructure, ending new petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and opposing new road building.

## Democracy and Rights
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post voting, votes for 16-year-olds, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, and defending the Human Rights Act.

## Immigration
The manifesto proposes ending the hostile environment policy, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## International
Proposals include increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI, supporting Ukraine, calling for bilateral ceasefire in Gaza-Israel conflict, ending UK arms exports to Israel, working toward EU rejoining, and signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons while working within NATO for reforms.

## Funding
Total additional spending would reach approximately £162bn revenue and £90bn capital by 2029-30, funded through taxation (estimated £172bn) and borrowing (estimated £79.5bn deficit).
